story.headline: Houthis strike Saudi base as Trump stays out
story.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed a drone and missile attack on Saudi Arabia's Sharurah base in retaliation for Saudi raids, as Trump declined Riyadh's plea to intervene.
story.display_body: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels claimed a drone-and-missile attack on a military base in southern Saudi Arabia on Sunday 13 September, calling it retaliation for repeated Saudi air raids in Yemen. The group's military spokesman, Yahya Saree, said the strike hit "weapons depots and command-and-control centres" at the Sharurah base, near the Yemeni border. It follows the Houthis' rapid advance this week along Yemen's Red Sea coast, where they consolidated control of the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait — the chokepoint at the southern mouth of the Red Sea — and closed it to Saudi tankers, the story that led yesterday's edition. Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government against the pro-Iranian fighters, preventively shut down a pipeline after the attacks, Swiss broadcaster SRF reported. Notably, US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would not intervene militarily: the US outlet Axios reported that de-facto Saudi ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had telephoned Trump twice on Thursday to ask him to strike the Houthis, and Trump said the Houthis had asked him to stay out of the war — a claim relayed on his own account, not independently confirmed. The UN migration agency (IOM) says more than 70,000 people have fled the fighting in western Yemen since the start of September.
story.why: with Iran already blockading the Strait of Hormuz (the Gulf's main oil chokepoint) for six months, the Houthi gains put Saudi Arabia at risk of losing its maritime outlets for oil at both ends of the peninsula — and Washington's public refusal to defend a core Gulf ally marks a notable shift in US posture.

story.headline: Russia's record drone barrage spills into Romania
story.summary: Russia fired 453 drones and missiles at Ukraine overnight and a drone crossed into NATO member Romania, which scrambled F-16s, while a Kyiv-Warsaw train was hit near Poland.
story.display_body: Russia launched one of its largest aerial barrages of the war overnight into Sunday 13 September — 453 attack drones and missiles, of which Ukraine said it destroyed or neutralised 405 drones and four missiles — and a Russian drone crossed into NATO member Romania, which scrambled two F-16 fighter jets. Romania's defence ministry said (in a communiqué reported by Le Monde) that the drone traversed Ukrainian and Moldovan airspace before heading toward the country's north-east; the jets took off from Borcea air base, a public alert was issued in Botoșani county, and forces later found a crashed flying object in a maize field near Botoșenița Mare, in neighbouring Suceava. Separately, the locomotive of a Kyiv–Warsaw passenger train was struck by a Russian drone in Volhynia, north-western Ukraine, about 2 km from the Polish border, the national railway Ukrzaliznytsia said via the Ukrinform agency; passengers were unhurt. Russian strikes on Odesa injured 20 people, and drone attacks killed at least two in the Zhytomyr region and one in Kherson. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said "the Russian barbarians are at your gates" and urged EU and NATO allies to "act now"; President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had fired roughly 2,100 long-range attack drones over the past week.
story.why: repeated drone incursions into Romanian and Moldovan airspace, and a strike this close to the Polish frontier, keep widening the war's spillover risk onto NATO and EU territory.

story.headline: Indonesian ferry missing in Java Sea storm
story.summary: The Virgo Transport 8, carrying more than 240 people, lost contact in bad weather in the Java Sea early Sunday; 103 were evacuated and about 140 remain missing.
story.display_body: An Indonesian passenger ferry carrying more than 240 people, the Virgo Transport 8, lost contact in bad weather in the Java Sea early on Sunday 13 September, and rescuers were searching for about 140 people after 103 had been evacuated. The vessel had sailed on Saturday from Surabaya, in East Java, toward South Kalimantan on Borneo when it lost contact at around 2 a.m., Indonesia's search-and-rescue agency (Basarnas) said; its Banjarmasin office received a distress report about two hours later and dispatched ships, a rescue team and a helicopter to the ship's last known position. Reuters reported that one person had died among those evacuated, while SRF later put the toll at six as the search continued. Indonesia, an archipelago of some 17,000 islands, relies heavily on ferries and suffers frequent, often deadly maritime accidents blamed on overcrowding and weak safety enforcement.

story.headline: Switzerland seeks to revive Ukraine peace talks
story.summary: Foreign Minister Cassis said Switzerland wants to reinvigorate Ukraine peace talks and hopes to host US-Russia-Ukraine negotiations in Geneva, after a security adviser's August trip to Kyiv and Moscow.
story.display_body: Switzerland wants to help "get peace talks moving again" on Ukraine, Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis said in an interview published Sunday 13 September, revealing that his security adviser, Gabriel Lüchinger, travelled to Kyiv and Moscow in August. Speaking to SonntagsBlick, Cassis said "we want to make a contribution to reviving peace talks," but gave no concrete results from Lüchinger's trip — "diplomacy is the drilling of thick boards; concrete results are the next steps, and they are secret." He recalled that he himself visited Kyiv and Moscow in February as chair of the OSCE (the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, a 57-state security forum), after which Switzerland supported US-led mediation between Russia and Ukraine in Geneva; both sides, he said, are "tired" after four and a half years of war. After President Zelensky named Switzerland as a possible venue for talks with the US and Russia, Bern hopes to host in Geneva, though the Federal Council has taken no decision on a peace conference: "Nothing is decided yet; we keep working persistently in the background — and everything can change." Cassis added that he has requested a meeting with his Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, on the margins of his coming trip to New York for the UN General Assembly, and that both the Russian and US foreign ministers "should come" to the OSCE ministerial conference Switzerland hosts in Lugano at year's end.
story.why: Bern is again offering its neutrality and good offices as a channel for Russia–Ukraine diplomacy — even as Russia mounts record drone barrages — though nothing concrete is yet on the table.

story.headline: Crans-Montana fires official over permit forgery
story.summary: The Valais municipality of Crans-Montana summarily dismissed a building-department employee accused of helping forge a construction permit for the Le Constellation bar, the site of a January fire.
story.display_body: The Valais municipality of Crans-Montana has summarily dismissed a building-department employee accused of helping to forge a construction permit for the "Le Constellation" bar, the site of a devastating fire on 30 January 2026. The application — for alterations to the bar's terrace, filed just weeks before the blaze — carried the name of a qualified engineer to meet formal requirements, but criminal investigators found the engineer had nothing to do with the project and that his name was used without his knowledge, allegedly with the knowledge of the municipal employee. Acting on the investigation's findings, the municipality said on Friday 11 September that the "relationship of trust ... is definitively destroyed" and terminated him with immediate effect.
story.why: it ties the paperwork behind a fire-hit venue to an alleged forgery inside the local building authority, raising questions about permit oversight in the run-up to the disaster.
